The
JAANCH Male Infertility Package by Thyrocare
is a specialised diagnostic screening package designed to evaluate important health and hormonal factors that may be associated with
male fertility problems
. Male infertility can have several possible causes, including hormonal imbalance, reproductive health conditions, lifestyle factors, certain medical conditions and nutritional issues.
The
Thyrocare JAANCH Male Infertility Package
may be useful for men who have been trying to conceive with their partner without success or who have been advised to undergo a fertility evaluation. Hormones play an important role in
sperm production, testosterone regulation and normal reproductive function
, and abnormalities in these markers may provide useful information during infertility assessment.
Male fertility problems may not always cause noticeable symptoms. However, some men may experience
reduced sexual desire, erectile difficulties, changes in testicular size, reduced facial or body hair, unexplained fatigue or other symptoms associated with hormonal imbalance
.
This package provides laboratory information that can support a broader male infertility evaluation. However, blood tests alone cannot determine every cause of infertility. Depending on the results and medical history, a doctor may also recommend
semen analysis, physical examination, ultrasound, genetic testing or other specialised investigations
.

available in serviceable locations for eligible blood tests, the JAANCH Male Infertility Package provides a convenient option for men looking for a
male fertility blood test, male infertility hormone test or reproductive health screening

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ's):
1. What is the JAANCH Male Infertility Package by Thyrocare?
The
Thyrocare JAANCH Male Infertility Package
is a specialised diagnostic package that evaluates important laboratory markers relevant to male reproductive and hormonal health. It can form part of a broader investigation when a couple is experiencing difficulty conceiving.
2. Who should consider the JAANCH Male Infertility Package?
The package may be considered by men who have been unable to conceive with their partner despite regular unprotected intercourse, have symptoms of hormonal imbalance, have known reproductive health concerns, or have been advised to undergo fertility testing by a doctor.
3. What can cause infertility in men?
Male infertility can have many possible causes, including problems with sperm production or quality, hormonal imbalance, varicocele, infections, genetic conditions, certain medications, smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, obesity and other lifestyle or medical factors.
4. Can hormone imbalance affect male fertility?
Yes. Hormones are involved in testosterone production and sperm development. Abnormalities in certain reproductive hormones may interfere with normal sperm production or sexual function, which is why hormonal assessment can be useful in selected infertility cases.
5. Is a blood test enough to diagnose male infertility?
No. Male infertility evaluation usually involves more than blood testing. A
semen analysis
is commonly an important part of fertility assessment because it evaluates factors such as sperm count, movement and morphology. Your doctor may recommend additional investigations depending on the findings.
6. When should a man get tested for infertility?
Fertility evaluation is commonly considered when pregnancy has not occurred after
12 months of regular unprotected intercourse
. Earlier evaluation may be appropriate when there are known fertility risk factors or when the female partner is 35 years or older.
7. Is fasting required for the Thyrocare JAANCH Male Infertility Package?
Preparation requirements depend on the exact tests included in the package. Follow the instructions provided with your
Thyrocare test booking
. Certain hormonal tests may also have preferred collection timings, so follow the recommended sample collection schedule.
8. Does the JAANCH Male Infertility Package include semen analysis?
Do not assume that semen analysis is included unless it is specifically mentioned in the current package test list. Blood-based fertility testing and semen analysis evaluate different aspects of male fertility and may both be recommended during an infertility work-up.
9. What should I do if my male fertility test results are abnormal?
Abnormal results should be discussed with a doctor, urologist, andrologist or fertility specialist. The results need to be interpreted alongside semen analysis, medical history, physical examination and other investigations before determining the possible cause of infertility.
10. Is Thyrocare home sample collection available for the JAANCH Male Infertility Package?
Thyrocare home sample collection
may be available for eligible blood investigations in serviceable locations. If semen analysis or another specialised sample is required, specific sample collection instructions or a centre visit may be necessary.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ's):
1. What is the Wellness Male Package?
Wellness Male Package is a comprehensive preventive health checkup package designed for men to screen lifestyle disorders, heart risk, cancer risk indicators and major organ health. It provides broad coverage through blood and urine tests to support early detection and better long-term health planning.
2. Who should opt for this package?
This package is ideal for men who want advanced preventive monitoring, those with stressful and sedentary lifestyle, irregular food habits, weight gain, fatigue, smoking or alcohol exposure, and people with family history of diabetes, cholesterol issues, thyroid imbalance or cardiac disease.
3. What tests are included in the Wellness Male Package?
The package includes Cancer Markers (2), Cardiac Risk Markers (5), Complete Hemogram (28), Complete Urine Analysis (24), Diabetes (3), Electrolytes (2), Iron Deficiency (5), Lipid (10), Liver (12), Pancreatic (2), Renal/Kidney (7), Thyroid (3), Toxic Elements (22) and Vitamin (2), giving complete preventive screening coverage.
4. Why does this package include cancer marker testing?
Cancer markers help in early preventive evaluation and risk screening. While they do not confirm cancer alone, they support early identification of abnormal trends and help doctors decide if further testing is needed.
5. What is the benefit of cardiac risk markers in this package?
Cardiac risk markers provide deeper insight into heart health and early cardiovascular risk. They help identify hidden inflammation and heart-related risk even before symptoms appear, making this package useful for lifestyle-related screening.
6. Why is toxic elements testing included in this package?
Toxic elements testing checks exposure to harmful metals and toxins that may enter the body through air, water, food or workplace environment. Monitoring these helps protect long-term organ health and supports better energy and overall wellness.
7. Is fasting required for the Wellness Male Package?
Yes, fasting of around
10–12 hours
is generally recommended for accurate results, especially for diabetes and lipid profile testing. Plain water is allowed during fasting.
